title: MC20 Sentinel-1 NESZ / thermal-noise implementation audit
hypothesis: The Experiment-0 VH overshoot (variance ratio 0.6963 -> 3.8023) is caused by an implementation, LUT-interpretation, registration, unit, or sub-swath handling error in the NESZ correction.
verdict_summary: REFUTED. The implementation was audited against the real SAFE product and verified correct on every axis tested. The VH behaviour is a legitimate physical property of this scene: cross-pol backscatter sits at the sensor's own noise floor.

experiment_0_recap.classification: MEASURED (prior task, reproduced bit-identically this task)
experiment_0_recap.note: Adding the below_noise_policy parameter did not perturb Experiment 0: re-running it produced identical numbers, because the default policy is the original behaviour.

safe_evidence.ipf_significance: The range x azimuth noise-vector combination rule applies from IPF 2.9 onward; this product at 3.52 is well past that threshold, so a product-level noiseAzimuthVectorList is expected and present.
safe_evidence.pixel_axis_note: The axis is NON-uniformly spaced (it inserts extra samples at sub-swath boundaries, e.g. ...8560 8600 8619 8620 8660...). scipy RegularGridInterpolator accepts non-uniform but monotonic axes, so this is handled correctly. The pre-existing calibration-LUT docstring's claim of 'regularly spaced' happens not to hold for the NOISE axis, but does not affect correctness.

polarization_binding_verified.note: Each noise XML's adsHeader/polarisation matches the polarization its filename claims -- no wrong-file / swapped-polarization bug.

subswath_coverage.note: No sub-swath boundary crosses the crop, so sub-swath selection cannot produce a discontinuity artifact here.

sources_consulted.supports: Noise vectors are provided in LINEAR POWER. Noise is subtracted from power-detected GRD data BEFORE the sigmaNought calibration factor is applied (Eq. 5-6: calibrated = A * [DN - eta*noiseLut]). This directly supports the implemented form sigma0_linear = (DN^2 - NoisePower) / sigmaNought^2.

documented_conflict_or_gap.issue: Neither ESA source consulted explicitly states that total noise = noiseRangeLut * noiseAzimuthLut (multiplication) as opposed to some other combination. SentiWiki describes range and azimuth contributions as separate computational steps without specifying the combination operator.
documented_conflict_or_gap.why_it_does_not_change_this_audit_s_conc: The azimuth LUT over this crop spans only 0.9996-1.1083, i.e. at most an 11% multiplicative effect. Whether it is multiplied, or omitted entirely, cannot produce the ~2.3x VH standard-deviation change observed. The VH result is therefore robust to this documentation gap.
documented_conflict_or_gap.recommended_follow_up: If the NESZ path is ever promoted toward production default, confirm the combination operator against the ESA S1 IPF product specification or the SNAP Sentinel1RemoveThermalNoiseOp source before doing so.

operations_traced.input_dn: uint16 DN read by direct file-seek from the real measurement TIFF, 1536x1536 crop at (top=7268, left=18657)
operations_traced.calibration_lut: parse_calibration_lut -> sigmaNought vectors, shifted into the crop's local frame by (row_offset, col_offset), bilinear via RegularGridInterpolator
operations_traced.range_noise_lut: parse_noise_lut -> noiseRangeLut, same shift-then-interpolate convention as the calibration LUT
operations_traced.azimuth_noise_lut: per-column sub-swath selection by full-scene range-sample span, then np.interp of that swath's noiseAzimuthLut over full-scene azimuth lines
operations_traced.nodata: DN == 0 forced to NaN (unchanged pre-existing convention)

bug_checks.B_lut_interpretation_bug: NOT FOUND -- LUT magnitudes (~300-490 over the crop) are in the same numeric regime as DN^2 (461-2609), which is the expected relationship for a linear-power noise LUT. An amplitude-vs-power confusion would have shown a square-root-scale mismatch (~19 vs ~370); it does not.
bug_checks.C_polarization_lut_mismatch: NOT FOUND -- each noise/calibration XML declares the polarization its filename claims (asserted in tests).
bug_checks.F_subswath_handling_error: NOT FOUND -- crop lies entirely inside IW3; uncovered columns raise rather than silently defaulting to a neutral factor (asserted in tests).

registration_verification.method: Independent manual bilinear reconstruction directly from the raw noise XML at a probe point, compared against the implementation's interpolated grid.
registration_verification.verdict: EXACT MATCH -- rules out off-by-one, crop-origin offset, absolute-vs-local line numbering, wrong swath offset, and wrong LUT dimensions.

corrected_implementation.change_made: Added below_noise_policy parameter to calibrate_to_db_denoised(). Default 'floor' preserves Experiment-0 behaviour exactly; new opt-in 'mask' marks below-noise pixels NaN instead of substituting an arbitrary 1e-6 constant.
corrected_implementation.physical_justification: Where the real, product-supplied noise power exceeds DN^2, sigma0 is UNMEASURABLE -- not 'very small'. Flooring substitutes an arbitrary constant (~-115 dB) that then dominates any statistic computed over those pixels. Masking is the honest representation and is consistent with the module's existing treatment of DN==0 border pixels (NaN) and with apply_netra_normalization()'s existing non-finite -> 0.0 nodata handling.
corrected_implementation.explicitly_not_a_score_driven_change: This change was made because flooring fabricates a value where none is measurable, NOT because it improves NETRA output. It is verified below to have ZERO effect on NETRA's input or output.

vv_findings.interpretation: VV signal sits comfortably above the noise floor (median SNR 6.2). Removing noise from a strong signal is a modest, well-conditioned correction: std rises 2.215 -> 2.888 dB and the variance ratio moves from 0.248 toward, but still below, 1.0. This is the expected, well-behaved outcome.

vh_findings.root_mechanism: The MEDIAN VH pixel carries only 7.9% more power than the sensor's own thermal-noise floor (SNR median 1.079), and the mean noise power is nearly identical between the two channels (VV 368.8 vs VH 371.3) because NESZ is a receiver-chain property, not a target property. VH's signal, however, is ~5.7x weaker than VV's. Subtracting a nearly-equal quantity leaves a small residual whose RELATIVE spread is enormous; in the logarithmic dB domain this inflates the standard deviation from 2.236 to 5.226 dB. The 'overshoot' past a variance ratio of 1.0 is therefore an arithmetic consequence of near-noise-floor subtraction, not an error.
vh_findings.why_this_is_expected_physics: Sentinel-1 cross-polarized (VH) backscatter over calm open water is well known to approach the instrument NESZ. A scene where ~44% of VH pixels fall below the noise floor is consistent with a low-wind / calm-sea acquisition, not with a processing defect.

noise_floor_analysis.headline_finding_retained: 43.8% of this MC20 crop's VH pixels have signal power at or below the sensor's own real, product-supplied thermal-noise floor. This finding is retained explicitly and is NOT diminished by the fact that it complicates the model story -- it is arguably the most important physical fact this audit established about the scene.
noise_floor_analysis.statistical_contamination_removed: All decision-relevant statistics are computed over physically meaningful populations only. The floor-contaminated VH variance ratio of 226.1 is retained in the record but explicitly labelled as an artifact of the arbitrary epsilon, never used for any conclusion.

spatial_analysis.method: 4x4 block means over the 1536x1536 crop, plus range-direction (column) and azimuth-direction (row) profiles.

range_direction_trend.note: Noise power decreases smoothly and monotonically with range, and the below-noise fraction follows it. This is the expected elevation-beam-pattern / range-spreading-loss behaviour.

spatial_analysis.verdict: SPATIALLY COHERENT, NOT LOCALIZED OR PATHOLOGICAL. The below-noise mask is near-uniform across all 16 blocks (0.40-0.47) with a smooth range-direction gradient and no discontinuities, no sub-swath seams, and no crop-boundary artifacts. A registration or indexing bug would be expected to produce exactly such artifacts; none are present.

VH.CONTAMINATED: std and mean dominated by the arbitrary -115 dB floor constant; not a physical measurement

critical_finding_B_equals_C_exactly.explanation: The floor policy produces ~-115 dB, which the frozen normalization clips to VH clip_low = -33.425 and rescales to exactly 0.0. The mask policy produces NaN, which apply_netra_normalization forces to the 0.0 nodata sentinel. BOTH COLLAPSE TO THE SAME VALUE. The corrected representation is therefore strictly a statistical-honesty improvement; it cannot and does not change what NETRA sees.
critical_finding_B_equals_C_exactly.significance: This forecloses any hope that a better below-noise representation would rescue detection under the frozen normalization contract.

nodata_sentinel_fraction_in_model_input.interpretation: This is the decisive result. NESZ correction drives 71.7% of the VH channel to the exact nodata sentinel value 0.0, versus 4.7% before correction and 2.585% in the training corpus. The physically-correct preprocessing makes MC20 MORE degenerate and FURTHER out of distribution from NETRA's perspective, not closer to it. Note 71.7% exceeds the 43.8% below-noise fraction because additional above-noise pixels still fall below the frozen VH clip_low of -33.425 dB after subtraction and are clipped to 0.

frozen_netra_behaviour.phase13_interpretation_discipline: Foreground fraction at the 0.806 operating threshold is 0.0 in all three conditions. Per Phase 13 this does NOT establish 'no oil at MC20'. The correct status remains OOD / DETECTION_UNAVAILABLE. Equally, the 1.67x probability rise from A to B/C is not 'improved detection' -- both values are ~5-6 orders of magnitude below threshold and the oil logit stays near -9.

root_cause.classification_from_phase1_list: G -- legitimate physical property of the scene (with the caveat that the arbitrary floor constant, a real but purely presentational defect, was separately identified and corrected)
evidence_for: Registration verified EXACTLY against independent manual reconstruction (0.0 difference).
Noise LUT magnitudes are in the correct numeric regime relative to DN^2, ruling out unit/amplitude-vs-power errors.
Polarization bindings verified correct in both noise and calibration XMLs.
Crop lies entirely within IW3; no sub-swath seam can contribute.
IPF 3.52 is consistent with the presence and use of a noiseAzimuthVectorList.

Below-noise mask is spatially coherent and near-uniform (0.40-0.47 across 16 blocks) with a smooth monotonic range-direction gradient tracking the noise power itself -- the signature of correct physics, not of an indexing bug.
VH median SNR is 1.079: the median VH pixel is only 7.9% above the noise floor, so near-equal subtraction mathematically must inflate relative (and hence dB) variance.
Mean noise power is nearly identical for VV and VH (368.8 vs 371.3) as expected for a receiver-chain NESZ, while VH signal is ~5.7x weaker -- fully explaining why only VH overshoots.
evidence_against: The ESA documentation consulted does not explicitly confirm the range x azimuth multiplication operator. This is recorded as an open documentation gap. However the azimuth factor spans only 0.9996-1.1083 over this crop, so no choice of operator could account for the observed ~2.3x VH std change.
root_cause.confidence: HIGH that no implementation bug is responsible for the VH overshoot. MEDIUM-HIGH that the scene is a genuinely calm/low-wind acquisition (inferred from cross-pol at NESZ; not independently confirmed against the ERA5 wind field available in MC20 Event Gold, which would be a cheap next check).

decision.reasoning: The audit's assigned question was whether the Experiment-0 NESZ correction is physically and implementation-wise correct. Every axis tested (A implementation, B LUT interpretation, C polarization mismatch, D registration, E units, F sub-swath) came back clean, with registration verified to exact numerical equality. The VH overshoot is explained by scene physics (cross-pol at the noise floor), not by a defect. But the correction does not restore NETRA's discriminative response -- and in fact drives 71.7% of the VH channel to the nodata sentinel, moving MC20 further from the training distribution. The implementation is valid; it is insufficient to resolve the OOD condition.
decision.why_not_A: No implementation bug was found; the one defect identified (the arbitrary floor constant) was presentational, affected statistics only, and is proven to have zero effect on model input or output.
decision.why_not_C_alone: The scene-specific physical effect (cross-pol at NESZ) is the MECHANISM behind the VH overshoot and is well supported, but selecting C alone would understate the operative conclusion, which is about sufficiency for the NETRA problem.
decision.why_not_D: 'Mixed calibration and domain effect' implies a calibration error contributing to the outcome. No calibration error was found.
decision.why_not_E: The question posed was resolved with high confidence on direct evidence.
decision.not_based_on_netra_score: This decision is supported by SAR-processing evidence (registration equality, LUT units, spatial coherence, SNR statistics). NETRA's output was used only as a diagnostic observation, per Phase 13.

next_netra_experiment.per_phase15_rule: Calibration is correct but NETRA remains OOD -> NEXT = training-domain expansion
next_netra_experiment.cheap_prerequisite_check_recommended_fir: MC20 Event Gold already contains a REAL ERA5 10m-wind field for this acquisition. Reading it to confirm or refute the calm-sea inference behind the cross-pol-at-NESZ explanation costs no new data and no training, and would raise the root-cause confidence from MEDIUM-HIGH to HIGH. Recommended before committing to data acquisition.
what_this_audit_rules_out_for_v0_3: Fixing MC20 by preprocessing correction alone -- proven ineffective here, and it worsens the nodata-sentinel fraction.
Expecting a better below-noise representation to help under the frozen normalization contract -- proven to collapse to the identical input.
Any explanation resting on a calibration or registration defect.
next_netra_experiment.constraint_carried_forward: The frozen v0.2 normalization contract (VH clip_low = -33.425 dB) is itself now implicated: noise-corrected cross-pol over calm water falls largely below that bound. If a v0.3 dataset ever adopts thermal-noise-removed inputs, the normalization statistics must be re-derived FROM TRAINING DATA under that same convention, as an explicitly disclosed, separately-versioned change -- never refitted from MC20.

future_data_requirements.product: GRD (IW), matching MC20's own product type
future_data_requirements.polarizations: VV + VH, with band semantics verified from each product's own annotation XML at ingestion rather than assumed
future_data_requirements.calibration_consistency: Sigma0-dB via the documented DN^2/sigmaNought^2 chain
future_data_requirements.thermal_noise_consistency: A SINGLE declared convention applied to training and inference alike -- this audit shows a train/infer mismatch in noise handling materially changes the input distribution
future_data_requirements.geographic_diversity: Beyond the Zenodo corpus's apparent ~55N Northern-European concentration
future_data_requirements.seasonal_diversity: Multiple seasons; Zenodo scenes carry no verified timestamps at all
future_data_requirements.sea_state_diversity: Must explicitly include calm / low-wind acquisitions where cross-pol approaches NESZ -- this audit shows that regime is where the current model fails, and it is likely under-represented in training
future_data_requirements.negative_examples: Clean-sea negatives in the same calm regime
